Subject: NUS School of Computing – Semester Exchange Placement AY2026/27 Sem 1 – Nominations Needed by March 10

Dear Colleagues,

The Office of Global Engagement is pleased to share that we have received confirmation of our exchange quota from NUS School of Computing (SoC) for Academic Year 2026/27, Semester 1 (August 2026 – December 2026).

QUOTA CONFIRMED: 2 places (up from 1 last cycle — thank you to the team for the relationship building).

About NUS SoC: Consistently ranked #1 in Asia for Computer Science (QS 2025), students at NUS SoC have access to modules in AI, systems, security, HCI, and software engineering. Our students in previous cycles reported the module quality and peer network as the highlights.

IMPORTANT ELIGIBILITY NOTES (please read carefully):
This exchange is for UG students only — NOT open to BTech students in their final year (they will not complete the exchange before graduation).
CGPA minimum: 7.5/10. NUS has enforced this strictly since last cycle — any nominee below 7.5 will be rejected at the NUS portal stage.
Priority given to students with CS/CSE/EE majors or with demonstrated CS coursework. Students from other majors are eligible but must demonstrate programming/CS competence in their statement.
Students must be enrolled at Plaksha for the semester AFTER return (i.e., Semester 2, 2026/27). Cannot be taken as a gap semester.

PROGRAMME COSTS:
No tuition fee to NUS (covered by the bilateral agreement). Students pay Plaksha fees as normal.
Living expenses in Singapore are significant — estimate SGD 1,500–2,000/month. No financial support from Plaksha or NUS for this exchange. Students must self-fund or apply for external scholarships (Plaksha Merit Scholarship may be applied concurrently — check with Finance).

TIMELINE:
Internal nomination deadline: March 10, 2026
OGE to submit nominations to NUS portal: March 20, 2026
NUS confirmation of acceptance: April 15, 2026

STUDENT APPLICATION PACKET (due to OGE by March 5 to allow review time):
1. Statement of purpose (why NUS SoC, which modules, what you hope to gain) – 500 words
2. Proposed module selections from NUS SoC catalogue (at least 6 modules listed, 4 confirmed preferred)
3. Latest Plaksha transcript
4. One academic reference from a CS/technical faculty member at Plaksha

INTERNAL APPROVAL:
Nominations go through our standard academic clearance process. OGE will coordinate with UG Academics and OAA. Program Chair sign-off is required given the module mapping.

Please note: NUS will not accept nominations submitted after March 20. No exceptions.

Warm regards,
Rohit Nair
Deputy Director, Global Partnerships
Office of Global Engagement, Plaksha University
